description: Two routes in the monitoring-visualization Flask app build SQL text with Python's '%' string formatting, splicing the attacker-controlled workflow_id URL segment directly into the query instead of binding it as a parameter. A workflow_id containing SQL metacharacters (documented PoC uses boolean-blind payloads like "AND '1'='0'" vs "AND '1'='1'") changes the query's meaning.

vulnerable_locations.notes: no earlier check gates this line on workflow_id matching a real workflow, so this one is directly reachable with an arbitrary URL value

vulnerable_locations.snippet: df_task_tries = pd.read_sql_query("""...WHERE task.run_id='%s' and try.run_id='%s'""" % (workflow_id, workflow_id), db.engine)
vulnerable_locations.notes: gated behind an earlier, safe ORM exact-match lookup (Workflow.query.filter_by(run_id=workflow_id)), so exploiting it via an arbitrary/nonexistent workflow_id from the URL is blocked in the default flow -- still genuinely SQL-injectable, and still part of the real fix commit, so it is graded too

fix_approach: Replace the '%'-formatted query strings with sqlalchemy.text(query) and pass workflow_id via a bound parameter (params={"run_id": workflow_id}) instead of splicing it into the SQL text.
out_of_scope: parsl/monitoring/queries/pandas.py has the identical '%'-formatting pattern across several helper functions (app_counts_for_workflow, nodes_for_workflow, resources_for_workflow, etc.) but was NOT touched by the real fix commit, and is not graded here -- only the two call sites inside views.py itself.
notes: Matched pair with the scitokens task: same vulnerability class (SQL injection via unparameterized string formatting), different project and exact code pattern, to check whether locate performance is consistent across similar-but-not-identical instances of the same bug class.
